findings.evidence: candidate.diff finish_task.py main(): `if prof == "multi-agent": reactivate_handed_off_board(integration, work, config)` before `published = subprocess.run(command, ...)`. specs/worktree-coordination/spec.md says 'Only the developer re-handoff entry (`finish`, also through `execute_requirement.py advance`) SHALL reactivate'. design.md 'Reactivation' bullet lists the terminal-path finish as well.
findings.summary: The candidate also reactivates a handed-off claim in the terminal publication path of finish, right before project_publish.py. The delta spec and the proposal name only the developer re-handoff entry (finish, also through advance) as allowed to reactivate. The design.md mentions the terminal path, but the worktree-coordination requirement 'Only the re-handoff entry reactivates a handed-off claim' does not. The spec and the code disagree on scope.

findings.evidence: candidate.diff finish_developer_handoff(): `reactivate_handed_off_board(integration, work, config)` is called immediately before `publish_pr(..., developer_handoff=True)`. Nothing re-hands-off the claim if publish_pr fails; hand_off_board runs only when `result == 0`.
findings.summary: The spec says reactivation happens after preflight passed and before publication. The candidate reactivates before publish_pr, and handoff_gates (routing, checkpoint and evidence gates) appear to run inside publish_pr for a developer handoff. If a gate fails, the claim stays reactivated, active and claiming scope, with no handed-off record. The spec does not define this state.
